summary: Alois Vaníček was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (1843–1847) and under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher (~1849/1850–1853). In 1882, he was Professor of Comparative Literature and Sanskrit at Charles University.

Alois Walde was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Innsbruck under Friedrich Stolz and studied at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien. He held professorships of comparative linguistics at Giessen (1909–1912), Innsbruck (1912), and Königsberg (1922–1924).

Aloysius Pieris worked in religious and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from institutions including London, Pontifical Theological Faculty of Southern Italy, Sri Lanka (Ph.D.), and Tilburg (Th.D.). He founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre (1974) and held chairs at Union, WTU, and Vanderbilt.

Alphonse François Lacroix was a linguist and religious studies scholar. He served as an agent for the Netherlands Missionary Society (1821), became a member of the London Missionary Society (1825), and founded the Bhowanipore Missionary Institution in 1851.
Alubomulle Sumanasara is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University under Yasuaki Nara.

Alva Noë is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oxford (~1986–1989) and Harvard University (~1989–1995). He held posts at the City University of New York (~1995–1996), UC Santa Cruz (~1996–2003), and UC Berkeley (~2003).

Alvan Clark Eastman worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning degrees from Harvard and New York University. He held positions at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and Detroit Institute of Arts, and directed museums in Evansville, Pasadena, Winnipeg, and Brooklyn.

Alvappillai Veluppillai worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics, studying at Ceylon and Oxford under Thomas Burrow. He held posts at the Universities of Ceylon, Peradeniya, and Jaffna, and was a guest or visiting professor at Uppsala, Kerala, and Arizona State.

Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1936–1937). He served as Director General of Archæology in India at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968) and as a UNESCO advisor (~1968–1973).
Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Olivier Lacombe, T. R. V. Murti, and Michel Hulin.

Amanda K. Goodman works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley, under Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.
Amar Nath Pandeya was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who held posts at the University of Delhi (attested 1968) and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (attested 1987).

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder, Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963), Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Shoryu Katsura, M. Fujimoto, and Alasdair Urquhart.

Amara Ali is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who held posts as Lecturer in Urdu at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (both attested 2026).

Amaranatha Jha studied at Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).
Amarasvar Thakur was an Indology scholar who held a post at the University of Calcutta (attested 1936) and served as General Editor of the Calcutta Sanskrit Series.

Amartya Sen is a philosopher and economist educated at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, and Cambridge. He held posts at Jadavpur, Calcutta, Delhi, the London School of Economics, and Harvard, where he was named Thomas W. Lamont University Professor and Professor of Economics and Philosophy (~2004).
Amaury de Riencourt was a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the Sorbonne, the University of Paris, and the University of Algiers, where he earned an M.A.

Amba Kulkarni is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Hyderabad (-2009). She served as Associate Professor and Head at Hyderabad (attested 2009–2026) and as a computational linguist at Dharmamitra (attested 2026).

Amber D. Carpenter works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under M. M. McCabe, Verity Harte, Raimond Gaita, Jonathan Lear, Susan Neiman, and Jonathan Glover. Her posts include positions at St Andrews, York, the Einstein Forum, Melbourne, and Yale-NUS College.
